name: TrustFS
description: This repository contains the source code, analysis scripts, and preprocessed datasets for the paper: "Good Prediction Does Not Imply Reproducible Feature Selection: A Stability, Equivalence, and Negative-Control Study Across 55 Binary Classification Tasks." Overview:Feature selection is widely used to build parsimonious predictive models and identify domain-specific biomarkers. This project investigates whether strong predictive performance (e.g., high ROC AUC) guarantees that the selected features are scientifically reproducible. Using an extensive evaluation across 55 binary classification tasks, we audited four feature selection methods: univariate F-test, mutual information, L1-penalized logistic regression, and correlation-pruned F-test. Our results reveal a stark disconnect: all selectors achieved strong discrimination, yet feature stability varied substantially. The L1 logistic selector exhibited the highest numerical accuracy but the lowest exact-identity stability. Repository Contents:1. trustfs_experiment.py: The core experimental pipeline. It performs outer cross-validation, stratified bootstrap perturbations, model fitting, and stability evaluations (Exact Jaccard, Matched Equivalence, and Negative Control intrusion).2. trustfs_analysis.py: The analysis and plotting script. It processes the raw outputs from the experiment script to generate the tables and figures (PNG, 600 DPI) presented in the manuscript.3.
